subject.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier

question: Should OpenClaw land this DSSE/Ed25519 hosted feed envelope verifier as the trust-boundary foundation before the config, refresh, and CLI visibility follow-up PRs land?
rationale: The code is now narrow and covered, but it defines how future hosted ClawHub feed bodies become trusted, which is a maintainer-owned security boundary rather than an automation-only correctness call.

options.title: Accept verifier slice now
options.body: Land this primitive as the approved foundation, then hold follow-up PRs to the same DSSE byte-verification, bounded-signature, and diagnostics privacy contracts.

options.title: Hold for stack-level review
options.body: Pause this PR until the RFC and config/refresh/visibility slices can be reviewed together as one trust-model decision.

options.title: Require a first consumer
options.body: Ask for the verifier to land with the first refresh/config consumer if maintainers do not want unused security primitives on main.

recommendation.title: Accept verifier slice now
recommendation.body: Land this primitive as the approved foundation, then hold follow-up PRs to the same DSSE byte-verification, bounded-signature, and diagnostics privacy contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is assigned on the live PR, authored the CI repair commit, and already reviewed the verifier protocol and bounds questions.
